BITUMEN LOGISTICS GUIDE
BITUMEN LOGISTICS & PACKAGING FOR IMPORT BUYERS

LAST REVIEWED SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 · PETROBIND EXPORT DESK

Packaging is a commercial decision, not a cosmetic one. For bitumen importers, the right format affects landed cost, unloading equipment, storage, safety, demurrage exposure, and whether the cargo can move through the selected port.

Request Bitumen Quote
View Bitumen Grades
CHOOSE PACKAGING BY SITE CAPABILITY FIRST

A buyer with heated storage, discharge pumps, and bulk receiving infrastructure can evaluate bulk or bitutainer routes. A buyer without that setup may need new steel drums, jumbo bags, or cartons so the shipment can be handled safely at destination.

New steel drums are practical for containerized imports and smaller project lots.

Jumbo bags, cartons, and blocks are often used for oxidized bitumen where solid handling is preferred.

Bitutainers and bulk shipments suit larger programmes with controlled heating and discharge infrastructure.

Flexitanks may be route and grade dependent, so PetroBind confirms suitability before quoting.

WHAT PETROBIND CHECKS BEFORE QUOTATION

Every RFQ is reviewed against product grade, loading origin, destination port, receiving method, order size, and requested Incoterm. This keeps the offer grounded in what can actually be packed, moved, cleared, and unloaded.

COMMON DOCUMENTS IN THE LOGISTICS FILE

A complete shipment file can include commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, COA, PDS, SDS/MSDS, and inspection documentation where required by the buyer or destination market.
